title: Neural motor control may be an exaptation of bioelectric navigation of morphospace

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Neural motor control may be an exaptation of bioelectric navigation of morphospace

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Neural control of body movement in three-dimensional space may be an evolutionary exaptation and speed-up of an older, slower role of bioelectric signalling: moving the body's configuration through anatomical morphospace during embryogenesis, repair and remodelling.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Neural networks control the movement of a body in three-dimensional space; this scheme may be an evolutionary exaptation and speed-optimization of a more ancient, slower role of bioelectrical signaling: the movement of body configuration through anatomical morphospace during embryogenesis, repair, and remodeling (Sullivan et al., 2016; Mathews and Levin, 2018; Mclaughlin and Levin, 2018).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin”. Scope: Evolution of nervous systems from developmental bioelectric signalling in animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.31

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative genomics can evaluate homology and timing of molecular components, but it poorly resolves whether neural motor control specifically exapted morphospace navigation. Existing data therefore address only molecular proxies.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the evolutionary history of neural and developmental bioelectric modules and test whether motor-control mechanisms are derived from homologous ancestral morphogenetic control circuits rather than independently recruited channel components.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exaptation of a system-level role is difficult to infer from shared components.

Relevant phenotypes leave no direct fossil record.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data existence: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.18

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ion-channel gene content can be compared across animals, and that comparison does not decide whether neural motor control is a sped-up reuse of developmental bioelectrics. The same molecules fit several evolutionary narratives. The claim is hedged as a scheme that may be an exaptation, and no public observation isolates that scheme.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Shared ion-channel genes are measurable, but exaptation of morphospace navigation into motor control is a historical path. Homology, convergence, and co-option all predict overlapping channels and leave the speed-up story untouched.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exaptation is an interpretation of conserved physiology.

No dataset records ancestral anatomical-navigation computations.
